fact: 第二次布尔战争于1899年10月11日爆发：布尔两国（德兰士瓦共和国与奥兰治自由邦）于1899年10月9日向英国发出最后通牒，要求撤走边境驻军，英方未接受，10月11日战争开始，至1902年5月31日结束。

sources.title: The Second Boer War 1899-1902 (angloboerwar.com)

fact: 1900年布尔战争出现关键转折：2月15日金伯利解围，2月28日被围近四个月的莱迪史密斯解围（英军先头部队2月28日入城，布勒将军3月1日骑马入城），英国本土的战争悲观情绪随之逆转。

sources.title: The Relief of Ladysmith, 28 February 1900 | National Army Museum
sources.quote: The Relief of Ladysmith, 28 February 1900 Chromolithograph, 1900. The Siege of Ladysmith was one of the most famous incidents of the Boer War (1899-1902).

sources.title: The Natal town of Ladysmith was relieved by General Sir Redvers Buller on 28 February 1900 (Ken Gillings, South African Military History Society)
sources.quote: The Natal town of Ladysmith was relieved by General Sir Redvers Buller on 28 February 1900, following the battle of the Thukela Heights, which was fought between 12 and 27 February. Buller rode into the town on 1 March 1900

fact: 马弗京于1900年5月17日解围（围城217天），消息经电报传到伦敦后，5月18日晚伦敦街头爆发大规模自发庆祝，报纸与人群的狂热庆祝使mafficking一词进入英语，成为布尔战争期间伦敦公共情绪的标志事件。

sources.title: Siege of Mafeking | History | Research Starters | EBSCOhost
sources.quote: Finally, on May 17, 1900, a relief force under the command of Colonel Bryan Mahon reached Mafeking. After 217 days the siege was lifted, and the Afrikaners retreated. When the news reached London, the city erupted in a celebration of patriotism mingled with relief. The word “mafficking” then entered the language

sources.title: Mafeking Night (davidandkay.me.uk social history)
sources.quote: Mafeking was relieved on Thursday 17th May but it took a day for the first rumours to reach England and several further hours before official confirmation, By the Friday evening huge crowds were on the London streets celebrating with boisterous rejoicing. Flags were everywhere. They were "mafficking", a word which survives in dictionaries.

fact: 1900年英国大选（俗称卡其大选）于9月26日至10月24日举行，正值布尔战争期间：保守党与自由统一党获402席（多数134席），自由党183席，新成立的劳工代表委员会获2席首次进入下议院，索尔兹伯里政府借战争氛围保住执政地位。

sources.title: 1900 United Kingdom general election - Wikipedia
sources.quote: The 1900 United Kingdom general election was held between 26 September and 24 October 1900, following the dissolution of Parliament on 25 September.

sources.title: UK History: The General Election of 1900 – Electoral Effects Of The Boer War
sources.quote: Contested in September-October, the Conservatives continued their landside albeit losing nine seats whilst Opposition Liberals gained six in a 402-183 result. Meanwhile, the newly-formed Labour Representation Committee ran its first election, winning two seats.

fact: 1889年伦敦码头大罢工确立的日工6便士（所谓docker's tanner）与加班8便士标准经谈判写入协议，此后成为伦敦码头日工工资的长期基准；按每周48小时折算约合1英镑4先令。该标准是1900年前后码头零工的主要工资参照，但当年实际出工时数与周收入尚无一手工资表核实。

sources.title: The 1889 London dockers' & tailors' strikes | London Museum
sources.quote: The demand for increased rates of pay to be 6d or 'tanner' ( around £2 now) per hour for day work with 8d per hour overtime resulted in the strike being referred to as the 'dockers' tanner'. ... The agreement conceded most of the dockers' demands, including the 'dockers tanner'.

fact: 查尔斯·布斯伦敦生活与劳动调查所复述的家庭预算显示：东区极贫阶层每名成人每周平均收入5先令1便士，其中房租1先令3便士、食物3先令7便士；贫困阶层每名成人周收入7先令7便士、房租1先令8便士。该数据来自19世纪末的调查（早于1900年约十年），只能作为1900年东区生存成本的量级参照。

sources.title: Early Innovations in Social Research: The Poverty Survey of Charles Booth (Bales, LSE Theses Online)
sources.quote: The average income per adult per week among the "very poor" was 5s 1d; rent would take 1s 3d of this and food a further 3s 7d.

fact: 中央伦敦铁路（今中央线）于1900年7月30日开通，连接Shepherd's Bush与Bank，全程实行2便士单一低廉票价，被称为Twopenny Tube；这一票价从一开始就使线路大受欢迎，并刺激了更多深层地铁线的修建，是1900年伦敦市内交通的主要新选择。

sources.title: Oxford Circus Underground Station at the north-east corner of Argyll Street and Oxford Street | Historic England
sources.quote: The railway, now part of the Central Line, received its Act of Parliament in 1891, and eventually opened in July 1900; its policy of charging cheap flat-rate fares, for which it became known as the 'twopenny tube', made the line extremely popular from the start, and encouraged the building of yet more deep-level lines.

sources.title: TfL celebrates the Central line's 125th anniversary with treasure hunt open to all at this year's Open House Festival
sources.quote: 30 July 1900 as a cross-London route from Shepherd's Bush to Bank.

fact: 在1905年《外国人法》之前，英国没有和平时期的入境管制：1852年英国外交大臣格兰维尔勋爵向各使馆发出的指示称，依当时英国法律所有外国人拥有不受限制地进入和居住于英国的权利；英国内政部的国籍史背景文件也确认英国第一部现代移民法是1905年《外国人法》。因此1900年的外国人入境和居住不需要签证、入境许可或口岸审查。

sources.title: Refugees: English Law's Protection or Persecution? (Prof. Leslie Thomas, Gresham College lecture, 2024)
sources.quote: From a practical perspective, therefore, between 1826 and 1905 there were no immigration controls as we know them today. The UK had open borders. In fact, the Foreign Secretary, Lord Granville, said in a directive to all British missions in 1852: "By the existing laws of Great Britain, all foreigners have the unrestricted right of entrance and residence in this country … No foreigner, as such, can be sent out of the country by the Executive Government"

sources.title: Historical background information on nationality (GOV.UK / Home Office)
sources.quote: The first modern immigration statute had been the Aliens Act 1905 which, as the title indicates, applied only to aliens (foreign nationals).

fact: 1870年《入籍法》规定外国人须在英国居住满五年（或在王室服务满相应年限）并具备良好品行方可申请入籍；入籍者取得与本土出生者基本相同的政治权利（包括进入议会和枢密院），并可拥有、继承和转让财产。未入籍的外国人仍可自由居住和持有财产，但不具备选举权等政治权利。

sources.title: Control of Enemy Alien Civilians in Great Britain (LSE Theses Online, U322824)
sources.quote: When the war began British nationality regulations derived from the Naturalisation Act of 1870 ... The act laid down a requirement of five year residence in Britain or crown service as qualifications for naturalisation, but it gave the subject the right to sit in parliament or on the Privy Council

sources.title: Naturalisation Papers (GENUKI / genguide)
sources.quote: Any alien living in Britain for more than five years who demonstrated good character gained the right to apply for naturalisation. Aliens were granted the ability to own, inherit, and transfer property.

fact: 1911年《大英百科全书》记载的伦敦证券交易所入会条件为：成员资格只有一年、须逐年重新当选；新成员由一名退任成员提名并须三名成员推荐、每人提供500英镑担保（自入会起四年），或由服务满四年的职员凭两名担保人入会；同一词条对比称纽约交易所成员必须是美国公民、巴黎交易所经纪人必须是法国公民，而伦敦条目所列的入会条件中没有国籍要求。注意：该记载成书于1911年，1900年交易所规则手册的原文细节尚未核对。

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica / Stock Exchange (Wikisource)
sources.quote: Membership of the Stock Exchange is for twelve months only; everyone without exception who wishes to remain a member must be re-elected annually ... The candidate must be recommended by three members, who also become sureties for him during the first four years from the date of his admission for £500 each. ... The New York Stock Exchange is a wealthy association consisting of members, who must be citizens of the United States ... Agents de change, who form the members of the official bourses in France, must be Frenchmen over twenty-five years of age

fact: 英国报业的制度性壁垒在1900年前已基本拆除：1695年出版许可法到期后下议院拒绝续期，报刊不再需要出版许可；1853年废除广告税、1855年废除报纸印花税、1861年废除纸张税，此后英国新闻界被视为拥有完全的出版自由。1900年办报不再需要政府许可，主要法律风险转向诽谤与内容责任。

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica / Press Laws (Wikisource)
sources.quote: On the expiration of the Licensing Act in 1692 it was continued till the end of the existing session of parliament (4 & 5 Will. and Mary, c. 24, §14). In 1695 the Commons refused to renew it.

sources.title: Lawrence GW (1954), University of Edinburgh (ERA)
sources.quote: The duty on advertisements was abolished in 1853, the duty was abandoned on newspapers in 1855, the duty on paper in 1861, and the optional duty on newspapers in 1870. So it is from that time that the British press may be said to date its complete freedom.

sources.title: An Overview of the Royal Mail Archive (The Postal Museum)
sources.quote: An act of 1855 abolished the compulsory payment of stamp duty on newspapers.

fact: 布尔战争爆发前后英格兰银行官方贴现率（Bank Rate）一周内两次上调：1899年10月3日由3%升至4%、10月5日再升至5%，11月底升至6%；1900年1月底回落至4%，此后整个战争期间维持在4%或以下。英格兰银行出纳部门档案将1899年10月的连续加息归因于与德兰士瓦的战争威胁及随之而来的黄金供应中断。

sources.title: The development of the role of the Bank of England as a Lender of Last Resort, 1870-1914 (Ogden)
sources.quote: Rumours of war in September and October 1899 had led to a drain on the Bank's reserve and to an increase in Bank Rate from 3% to 4% per cent on October 3rd and to 5 per cent on October 5th. This was followed by an increase to 6 per cent at the end of November, but these relatively high rates did not continue: by late January 1900 Bank Rate stood once again at 4 per cent and generally remained at or below this level for the duration of the war.

sources.title: Bank of England Staff Working Paper No.718: Monetary policy spillovers in the first age of financial globalisation (Georgina Green, 2018)
sources.quote: just before the outbreak of war in South Africa in October 1899, the Cashier Department recorded the "extraordinary circumstances of two advances in Bank Rate in one week ... due to threatened war with Transvaal and consequent stoppage of gold supplies"

fact: 1900年前后伦敦证券交易所的交易渠道：公众必须通过交易所成员（broker）下单，成员分为面向公众的broker与只与其他会员报价成交的jobber（做市商）；成交按半个月结算交割（正常间隔14天），成交价刊入official list，营业时间为上午11时至下午3时30分、周六至1时30分（1911年百科称营业时间自早年几乎未变）；英国国债如consols等可以现金（money bargain）即时交易，多数其他证券则只能按结算日交割。

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica / Stock Exchange (Wikisource)
sources.quote: The London Stock Exchange is remarkable for having developed spontaneously a special mode of doing business, namely the differentiation of members into jobbers and brokers. A jobber is a member of the Stock Exchange who, according to the rules of that body, does business only with other members, as opposed to a broker who does business with the public as well as with his fellow members. ... The interval between two settlements varies from 12 days to 19 days, but the normal interval is 14 days ... In most securities it would not be easy to deal "for money" ... but this can always be done in consols and other British government securities

fact: 南非战争头两年（1899—1901），英国国库券（Treasury bills）对投资者是罕见机会：据1911年《大英百科全书》记载，当时可以买入价格相当于在票据存续期内年化3¾%收益率的英国国库券，巴黎的大型银行机构也是英国国库券的常客。

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica / Stock Exchange (Wikisource)
sources.quote: They are often large purchasers of British Treasury bills, which during the first two years of the South African War afforded an extraordinary opportunity to the investor, it being possible to buy them at prices yielding a rate equal to 3¾% per annum during the currency of the bills.

fact: 1900年8月8日获御准的《1900年公司法》规定：向公众募集的股份，除非招股说明书列明的最低认购额已足额认购且申请款已实收，否则不得分配；每股申请款不得低于面值的5%；招股说明书须在发表前送注册官登记并由全体拟任董事签署；该法除另有规定外自1901年1月1日起施行。这意味着1900年当年发行的新股招股仍处于旧规则与新规则交替期。

No allotment shall be made of any share capital of a company offered to the public for subscription, unless the following allotment conditions have been complied with, namely,— (a) the amount (if any) fixed by the memorandum or articles of association and named in the prospectus as the minimum subscription upon which the directors may proceed to allotment ... fact: 《每日邮报》1896年5月4日创刊于伦敦，是定价半便士的大众日报；多数资料称到1900年前后其日发行量已达约100万份，成为当时全球销量最大的日报，标志着英国廉价大众报业（出版业）的成型。另有资料称1899年发行量54.5万份、1902年才突破100万，发行量口径存在差异。

sources.title: Early Edition: the Daily Mail, British newspapers, and the moving image, 1896-1922 (Tom Rice, University of St Andrews)
sources.quote: The first edition of the Daily Mail on May 4 1896 included an advertisement for the "latest scientific marvel,"the Lumiere Cinematograph. ... The concurrent growth of the Daily Mail –which with a daily circulation of one million by 1900 was the largest selling newspaper in the world –is the most striking example of a new popular,affordable press.

sources.title: The History of Newspapers (archive.org)
sources.quote: In 1896, the brothers Alfred and Harold Harmsworth, who were great pioneers of news-papers, established the 'Daily Mail' as a popular, half-penny newspaper. The paper introduced many new ideas, and was an instant success. By 1900 it had a circulation of over one million copies every day.

sources.title: The Daily Mail (London, UK) - Conrad (conradfirst.net)
sources.quote: The Daily Mail's circulation rose to 545,000 by 1899, more than one million in 1902 (then the world's largest), and 1,390,000 by 1914.

fact: 哈姆斯沃思报业的后续结果：到1921年，哈姆斯沃思三兄弟（北岩爵士、罗瑟米尔勋爵与莱斯特·哈姆斯沃思爵士）旗下报纸合计日发行量超过600万份，包括《泰晤士报》《每日邮报》和《每日镜报》，证明半便士大众报业模式在20多年里带来了持续的规模扩张与报业集中。

sources.title: The United Kingdom | Encyclopedia.com
sources.quote: the three Harmsworth brothers, Lords Northcliffe and Rothermere and Sir Lester Harms-worth, in 1921 owned among them newspapers attaining more than 6 million in aggregate circulation, including _The Times_, the _Daily Mail_, and the _Mirror_.

fact: 1900年英国登记商船约占世界商船总吨位的45%，英国船队主导全球海运贸易，此后这一比例开始缓慢下降。航运是当时英国最大的产业部门之一，伦敦港的码头、船运与相关服务业构成外国人在伦敦谋生的重要产业背景。

sources.title: The Decline of British Shipping: Some New Perspectives (Davies, PhD thesis, University of Warwick, WRAP)
sources.quote: In terms of British registered shipping as a proportion of the world fleet, a decline can be noted from 1900 which was when British-registered shipping dominated global commerce and provided 45% of world tonnage (Sturmey, 1962).
